figures.label: 圖
figures.caption: 圖：放學後的咖啡店
figures.description: 平日下午的一家咖啡店裡，幾乎每張桌子都坐著穿制服的高中生。他們戴著耳機，桌上攤開課本、講義與筆記型電腦，每人旁邊都放著一個已經喝完的空杯子。靠窗的長桌上，一條延長線同時替好幾台筆電充電；角落有兩名學生正小聲討論一道數學題。一位拿著咖啡的上班族站在門口張望，找不到空位。店門的玻璃上貼著告示：「平日限時兩小時」。

questions.stem: 提示：放學後或週末，越來越多高中生選擇帶著課本和筆電到咖啡店讀書，而不是待在家裡。請根據下圖，寫一篇英文作文，文分兩段。第一段描述圖中咖啡店裡的情景；第二段說明學生喜歡到咖啡店讀書的原因，以及這種現象可能對學生本身或店家帶來的影響。

1.explanation_zh: 第一段只要描述圖中的咖啡店，不必急著評論；第二段有兩個任務：原因與影響，兩者都要寫到。影響可以是對學生（花費、讀書效率）或對店家（座位被長時間占用、因此限時），只寫原因、沒寫影響，內容分數會被扣。
evidence: 第一段描述圖中咖啡店裡的情景
這種現象可能對學生本身或店家帶來的影響
1.strategy_zh: 圖中的「平日限時兩小時」告示和找不到位子的上班族，正好可以當作「對店家的影響」的線索。
hints: 第一段：從整間店寫到門口的告示，至少寫四個細節
第二段前半：兩個原因，其中一個用自己的經驗說明
第二段後半：寫一項對學生、一項對店家的影響，最後提出你的態度

moves.zh: 描述圖中咖啡店裡的情景
說明學生喜歡到咖啡店讀書的原因
這種現象可能對學生本身或店家帶來的影響

content.focus_zh: 第一段要寫出圖中的幾個重點（坐滿的學生、空杯子、找不到位子的上班族、限時告示）；第二段要有至少兩個原因與至少一項影響（對學生或對店家），最好用自己讀書的經驗或具體數字撐住原因與影響。

bands.descriptor_zh: 回應題目的每一項要求，主旨明確；用具體的事例、細節或親身經驗撐起每個重點。
大致回應題目，但有一項要求寫得單薄，或細節偏籠統、說服力不足。
漏掉題目的主要要求或主旨模糊，多數句子空泛、重複或偏離題目。
空白、離題、只抄題目，或內容少到無法判斷要說什麼。

organization.focus_zh: 第一段由整體（店裡坐滿學生）寫到細節（空杯、延長線、門口告示）；第二段先寫原因、再寫影響，原因和影響之間要用轉承語清楚換軌。

bands.descriptor_zh: 兩段分工清楚，各有主題句；句與句、段與段的銜接自然，轉承語用得恰當，篇幅分配合理。
段落大致分明，但有的地方跳接或重複，轉承語偏少或用得生硬。
重點排列混亂，前後句常接不起來，讀者不容易跟上。
看不出段落與順序，句子彼此無關。

grammar.focus_zh: 描述圖片用現在進行式與現在完成式（have stayed），說明原因時注意 because、since 子句的完整性；動名詞當主詞（Studying in cafés …）後面的動詞用單數。

bands.descriptor_zh: 句子幾乎沒有文法、標點錯誤，能交替使用簡單句、複句與不同的句首。
偶有時態、單複數或標點錯誤，但讀得懂意思；句型變化有限。
錯誤多到常讓人誤解意思，句子結構常不完整。
幾乎沒有正確的句子，無法理解。

vocabulary.focus_zh: 讀書與店家相關的字（focus、distraction、customer、limit、income）要用得準，避免一直重複 study 與 good。

bands.descriptor_zh: 用字精準、貼切，搭配自然，少有重複；拼字與大小寫幾乎全對。
字彙範圍偏窄、常重複同幾個字，偶有用字不當或拼錯，但不妨礙理解。
用錯字或拼錯字很多，常讓人看不懂。
幾乎每個字都用錯或拼錯，無法理解。

rubric.deductions_zh: 字數明顯不足（少於 100 個單詞）或沒有分成兩段，各扣總分 1 分；兩種情形同時發生只扣 1 分。離題或空白以 0 分計。

model_texts.label: steady
model_texts.text:
The picture shows a busy coffee shop after school. Almost every table is taken by students in school uniforms. Most of them are wearing earphones, and their textbooks and computers are spread out in front of them. Each student has an empty cup beside the books, which shows that they have stayed there for a long time. Meanwhile, an office worker with a cup of coffee is standing at the door, but he cannot find a seat. There is also a sign on the door saying that customers can stay for only two hours on weekdays.
There are several reasons why students like to study in coffee shops. First, there are fewer distractions in a coffee shop than at home, where it is easy to take a nap or turn on the TV. Second, being around other hard-working people makes it easier to focus. For example, when I studied at home last month, I kept checking my phone. However, at a coffee shop near my school, I finished a whole chapter of history in one afternoon. Studying in coffee shops also has some effects. Students may spend too much money on drinks, and shop owners may lose other customers because their tables are always full. As a result, some shops now limit how long people can stay. In conclusion, coffee shops can be good places to study, but students should respect the rules and other customers.

paragraphs.function_zh: 描述圖片：咖啡店坐滿讀書的學生，並寫出空杯、上班族與限時告示

paragraphs.topic_sentence: There are several reasons why students like to study in coffee shops.

self_assessment.explanation_zh: 描述完整，原因兩項都有說明、其中一項有自己的經驗，影響也兼顧學生與店家（內容 4）；兩段各有主題句，列舉與因果轉承清楚，但影響部分稍短（組織 4）；句子正確，有動名詞主詞與非限定 which 子句（文法句構 4）；用字正確、以常用字為主（字彙拼字 3）。總分 15，屬穩健版。

model_texts.label: top
model_texts.text:
On a weekday afternoon, the coffee shop in the picture looks more like a library than a place to relax. Nearly every seat is occupied by high school students in uniform, each wearing earphones and surrounded by textbooks, handouts, and a laptop. Their cups, however, have long been empty, a sign that they ordered one drink hours ago and have stayed ever since. Apart from the hum of the coffee machine, the only sound is the soft clicking of keyboards. At the long table by the window, a single power strip is charging several laptops at once, while in the corner two classmates are whispering over a math problem. The only person who seems out of place is an office worker holding a coffee at the entrance, searching in vain for an empty chair. Right beside him, a notice on the glass door makes the shop’s position clear: customers may stay for only two hours on weekdays.
For many teenagers, ordering a drink and claiming a corner seat has become an after-school ritual, mainly because a café offers a balance that home cannot. At home, the bed, the TV, and the refrigerator are constant temptations, whereas a coffee shop provides just enough background noise to keep the mind alert. Moreover, studying among strangers creates a gentle pressure; when everyone around you is working, scrolling through social media suddenly feels embarrassing. I discovered this last semester before my midterm exams. After two wasted evenings at my desk, I moved to a small café near my school. The change doubled my productivity: within three hours, I had reviewed an entire chapter of chemistry. Nevertheless, this habit has costs that are easy to overlook. For instance, a student who visits a café four times a week may spend over NT$1,500 a month on drinks, money that could have bought several reference books. Shop owners, on the other hand, face a real dilemma: they welcome young customers, but a table occupied for an entire afternoon brings in little income, which explains the two-hour limit in the picture. In the long run, more cafés may set stricter rules or even charge for seats. In short, students who enjoy this kind of space should be considerate customers and treat it as a shared place rather than a free study room. After all, ordering a second drink or leaving on time is a small price for keeping it open to everyone.

paragraphs.function_zh: 描述圖片：用「像圖書館」定調，再用空杯、延長線、門口的上班族與告示把場景寫具體

paragraphs.function_zh: 原因＋影響：兩個原因配合期中考前的經驗，再分別寫對學生（花費）與對店家（兩難、限時）的影響，最後提出使用者應有的態度
paragraphs.topic_sentence: For many teenagers, ordering a drink and claiming a corner seat has become an after-school ritual, mainly because a café offers a balance that home cannot.

self_assessment.explanation_zh: 描述生動且有推論（空杯代表待很久），原因有經驗佐證，影響兼顧學生與店家並有數字（內容 5）；原因、經驗、代價、店家、結論層次分明，轉承多樣（組織 5）；分詞構句、同位語、could have p.p.、非限定子句運用自然且正確（文法句構 5）；用字精確（temptations、dilemma、considerate），偶有較長的名詞片語（字彙拼字 4）。總分 19，屬頂標版。

steady.comment_zh: 第一段寫到坐滿的學生、耳機與課本、空杯、找不到位子的上班族與限時告示，題目要點齊全；第二段兩個原因加自己在家與在咖啡店讀書的對比經驗，再寫對學生（花錢）與店家（流失客人、限時）的影響。全文無語言錯誤；由原因轉到影響只用 Studying in coffee shops also has some effects. 一句，換軌略生硬；coffee shop(s) 重複六次、結尾用 good places，字彙範圍中等。

top.comment_zh: 描寫生動（looks more like a library、searching in vain），第二段原因、親身經驗、金額估算（NT$1,500）、店家兩難與兩小時限制前後呼應，結尾提出做體貼顧客的看法，內容與組織俱佳；句型與字彙（temptations、dilemma、considerate）都在高水準。小瑕疵：the only sound is the soft clicking of keyboards 與後一句 two classmates are whispering 互相矛盾（耳語也是聲音），且咖啡機的聲音是圖中沒有的細節，建議改成 the loudest sound 或刪去 only。

steady.comment_zh: 第一段涵蓋坐滿的學生、耳機、空杯、上班族與兩小時告示；第二段有兩個原因（較少干擾、同儕效應）與對學生、店家的影響，並用自己的讀書經驗支持，結尾提醒要守規則。文法與拼字都正確，組織清楚；用字偏口語平實（good places、some effects），細節比較籠統，因此字彙給 3。

top.comment_zh: 第一段由整體（像圖書館的咖啡店）寫到延長線、討論數學題的學生、站在門口的上班族與告示，細節完整；第二段原因、親身經驗、金額、店家兩難與長遠影響層次分明，轉承語（Moreover、Nevertheless、on the other hand）使用恰當。句型與字彙都很豐富且無錯誤；Ordering a drink and claiming a corner seat has become 把兩個動作視為同一個儀式用單數動詞，可接受但較嚴格的評分者可能會挑。
